ios.body: App Total New Subs is -3.4% and App Total Install is +6.3%; the gap between them (-9.7pp) is under the 10pp we treat as a real signal, so the share of people who install and then subscribe is close to normal. New subs start as 7-day free trials, so today's new subs are next period's App Total Revenue. So nothing unusual is building up that would swing App Total Revenue in about 7 days.

insights.title: Next period outlook — Expect App Total Revenue to weaken in about 7 days — fewer of the people installing are subscribing, mostly YCP.
insights.body: App Total New Subs is -16.6% while App Total Install is +3.9% — fewer of the people who installed are subscribing (-20.4pp less growth). New subs start as 7-day free trials, so today's new subs are next period's App Total Revenue. So expect App Total Revenue to weaken in about 7 days. App Total Revenue is +2.0% right now, so expect that to cool off. Most of the fall comes from YCP (-36.5%); YMK is -3.7%.

insights.title: Market trend — YCP is losing ground fast on turning installs into subs (-35.0%, now 8.1%).
insights.body: In YCP, 8.1% of installs now turn into new subs — -35.0% versus last period. It is about 41% of revenue (a big revenue market): fewer of the people downloading are subscribing, and revenue will feel that within a week or two.

insights.title: Revenue vs new subs — App Total Revenue +11.2% does not match new subs -2.9% from 7 days earlier — this growth is not coming from new customers.
insights.body: App Total Revenue on 10-04 vs 09-27 is +11.2%, but App Total New Subs on 09-27 vs 09-20 was -2.9% — they moved in opposite directions. Most new subs start as a 7-day free trial, so the revenue landing now mostly comes from people who subscribed about 7 days ago. Since those subs went the other way, this growth is coming from existing customers instead: check renewals and cancellations, refunds, or a recent price change — not marketing or installs.

insights.title: Installs to subs, by app — YMK is turning installs into New Subs worse than usual (-3.7% vs Install +6.1%).
insights.body: Some apps are not converting installs into subscribers at their usual rate: YMK New Subs -3.7% vs Install +6.1% (worse than its installs); YCP New Subs -36.5% vs Install +1.1% (worse than its installs). Revenue follows about a week later, so these are the apps to watch next week.

insights.title: Which app — App Total Install +3.9% is mostly YMK — not every app.
insights.body: App Total Install moved +3.9% overall, but the apps are far apart (All App +3.9%, YMK +6.1%, YCP +1.1%, YCV +2.8%). YMK accounts for most of it, so look at what changed in that one app rather than something affecting all of them.

insights.title: Which country — US is out of line with every other country on App Total New User (+11.6% vs +2.9%).
insights.body: For All App, App Total New User in US is +11.6% while all countries together are +2.9% — a gap of +8.7pp. US is about 39% of revenue, so it is big enough to be worth a look.

insights.title: Install source — App Total Install +3.9% — Paid Install is behind most of it (+1,478, +9.5%).
insights.body: App Total Install was 36,784, against 35,416 for the average of the same weekday over the past 4 weeks — a change of +1,368. Where that came from: Paid Install +1,478 (+9.5%), Organic Install -728 (-4.2%), SEO Install +702 (+37.7%). Paid Install moved the most on its own (+1,478, +9.5%) and is now 46.5% of all installs, so that is the channel to look at first. Going the other way at the same time: Organic Install -728.
